name: StarterGui
simple: StarterGui is where you build your game's on-screen UI (buttons, health bars, menus) in Studio. When a player's character spawns, everything in StarterGui is copied into that player's own PlayerGui, which is what they actually see. It also has methods to hide or change Roblox's built-in UI, like the chat, the player list, and the backpack bar.
analogy: StarterGui is like the master copy of a worksheet on the teacher's desk. Each student (player) gets their own photocopy (PlayerGui) to write on. Writing on the master copy during class doesn't change the copies students already have.
whenToUse: Design ScreenGuis (buttons, text, menus) in Studio that every player should get.
Hide Roblox's built-in UI, like the player list or the backpack hotbar (SetCoreGuiEnabled).
Show a little notification in the corner (SetCore "SendNotification").
where: A service in the Explorer. Get it with `game:GetService("StarterGui")`. Put ScreenGuis inside it in Studio. Call SetCore, GetCore, SetCoreGuiEnabled and GetCoreGuiEnabled from a LocalScript, because they change one player's screen.

terms.UI / GUI: User interface: the buttons, text, pictures and menus drawn on the screen.
terms.ScreenGui: A container for 2D UI that draws on the player's screen. Put buttons and labels inside it.
terms.PlayerGui: A folder inside each Player that holds the UI that player actually sees. Filled with copies from StarterGui.
terms.CoreGui: Roblox's own built-in UI: chat, player list, backpack hotbar, health bar, emotes menu, and the top bar.
terms.ResetOnSpawn: A property on ScreenGui. If true (default), that ScreenGui is deleted and re-copied every time the character respawns. If false, it's copied once and stays.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI scripts are LocalScripts.
terms.Enum.CoreGuiType: The list of built-in UI pieces you can turn on or off, like PlayerList, Backpack, Chat, Health, EmotesMenu, or All.
terms.pcall: Runs a function safely: if it errors, your script keeps going. Useful for SetCore, which can fail if Roblox's UI hasn't loaded yet.
terms.yield: Pause and wait. GetCore can pause your script for a moment.

examples.title: How StarterGui gets to the player's screen
examples.place: LocalScript inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

-- This script was COPIED from StarterGui into the player's PlayerGui.
-- script.Parent is the copy of the ScreenGui the player sees.
local screenGui = script.Parent
print(screenGui:GetFullName()) -- e.g. Players.YourName.PlayerGui.ScreenGui

-- If screenGui.ResetOnSpawn is true (the default), this whole ScreenGui
-- (and this script) is deleted and copied fresh every respawn.
-- Set it to false to keep things like scores on screen across deaths.
screenGui.ResetOnSpawn = false
explain: In Studio you build the UI inside StarterGui. That's the template.
When a character spawns, Roblox copies StarterGui's children into that player's PlayerGui. The copy is what shows on screen.
Because of the copy, script.Parent is the player's own ScreenGui, not the one in StarterGui.
ScreenGuis with ResetOnSpawn = true are replaced every respawn. With false, they are copied once and stay.
To change what one player sees during the game, change their PlayerGui, not StarterGui.

examples.title: Hide the player list and show a notification
examples.code:
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")

-- Hide the built-in player list in the top-right corner
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.PlayerList, false)

-- SetCore can fail if Roblox's UI isn't ready yet, so try a few times
local success = false
for attempt = 1, 5 do
    success = pcall(function()
        StarterGui:SetCore("SendNotification", {
            Title = "Welcome!",
            Text = "Reach the top to win.",
            Duration = 5, -- seconds
        })
    end)
    if success then
        break
    end
    task.wait(1)
end
explain: SetCoreGuiEnabled turns a built-in UI piece on or off for this player.
SetCore("SendNotification", {...}) pops up a small message at the bottom right.
We use pcall and retry because SetCore errors if Roblox's own UI scripts haven't loaded yet.

gotchas: Changing StarterGui while the game runs doesn't change what players already see. Edit player.PlayerGui instead (or wait for them to respawn).
SetCore, GetCore and SetCoreGuiEnabled must be called from a LocalScript.
SetCore can error if called too early. Wrap it in pcall and retry.
If Players.CharacterAutoLoads is false, StarterGui isn't copied until the character is loaded with LoadCharacterAsync.
The top bar can't be hidden with SetCoreGuiEnabled. Use SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false).

StarterGui.ClipsDescendantsSupportsRotat.simple: A Studio setting (scripts can't change it). When on, a frame with ClipsDescendants also correctly cuts off rotated things inside it.

StarterGui.ProcessUserInput.simple: Hidden, plugin-only. Lets StarterGui handle input like PlayerGui does. Not used by game scripts.

StarterGui.RtlTextSupport.simple: A Studio setting (scripts can't change it). Turns on right-to-left text layout for languages like Arabic and Hebrew. On by default.

StarterGui.ScreenOrientation.simple: The screen direction phones and tablets start in: landscape (sideways), portrait (upright), or Sensor (follows how they hold the device, the default). Changing it later doesn't affect players already in the game; change their PlayerGui.ScreenOrientation for that.

StarterGui.ShowDevelopmentGui.simple: Whether StarterGui's UI is shown in the Studio editor while you build. Doesn't affect the running game.

StarterGui.VirtualCursorMode.simple: A Studio setting (scripts can't change it). Turns the gamepad virtual cursor on or off, which lets controller players move a pointer over buttons. Always on in VR.

StarterGui:GetCore.simple: Reads a setting or info from Roblox's built-in UI, picked by name, like "PointsNotificationsActive" or "GetBlockedUserIds". Use it in a LocalScript. It may pause briefly.
StarterGui:GetCore.example:
-- LocalScript
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
local blocked = StarterGui:GetCore("GetBlockedUserIds")
print("You have blocked " .. #blocked .. " users")

StarterGui:GetCoreGuiEnabled.simple: Tells you if a built-in UI piece (like the Backpack or PlayerList) is turned on. Call it in a LocalScript.

StarterGui:SetCore.simple: Changes or uses a feature of Roblox's built-in UI, picked by name. Popular ones: "SendNotification" (pop-up message), "ResetButtonCallback" (false turns off the reset button), "TopbarEnabled", "PromptSendFriendRequest". Use in a LocalScript, wrapped in pcall.
StarterGui:SetCore.example:
-- LocalScript: turn off the Reset Character button
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
pcall(function()
    StarterGui:SetCore("ResetButtonCallback", false)
end)
StarterGui:SetCore.gotcha: It errors if Roblox's UI scripts haven't loaded yet. Retry with pcall and task.wait.

StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled.simple: Turns a built-in UI piece on or off for this player: chat, player list, backpack hotbar, health, emotes menu, or All. Call it in a LocalScript.
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled.example:
-- LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts: make your own inventory instead
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack, false)
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled.gotcha: It can't hide the top bar. Use SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false) for that.
